To use the cloud features of Square Orb Gallery (such as Google Photos import or Adobe Lightroom CC integration), you need to establish a secure connection between your WordPress site and these services. This is done through "developer accounts," which serve as a digital bridge, ensuring that only your specific website can access your private cloud assets.

### Why Do I Need a Developer Account?

Cloud services like Google and Adobe protect your personal photos and data behind high-security gates. To let your website "talk" to these services, you must register your site as an official application. By creating a project in their respective Developer Consoles, you receive unique keys (Client IDs and Secrets) that identify your site as a trusted entity.

Without these, your website has no permission to request your media, and the cloud services will deny any attempts to connect for security reasons.

- [Setting up your Adobe Developer Account](https://awesomediscoveryzone.com/auragallery/docs/aura-gallery/cloud-integration-media/setting-up-your-adobe-developer-account/)

- [Setting up your Google Developer Account](https://awesomediscoveryzone.com/auragallery/docs/aura-gallery/cloud-integration-media/setting-up-your-google-developer-account/)

### Creating Authentication Credentials

After setting up your developer account, you can create the necessary credentials:

- [Create a Google OAuth Client ID and Secret](/auragallery/docs/aura-gallery/cloud-integration-media/create-a-google-oauth-client-id-and-secret/)

- [Create a Google Vision API Key](/auragallery/docs/aura-gallery/cloud-integration-media/create-a-google-vision-api-key/)

- [Create an Adobe Client ID and Secret](/auragallery/docs/aura-gallery/cloud-integration-media/create-an-adobe-client-id-and-secret/)

<FAQ title="What cloud storage services does Square Orb Gallery support?">
Square Orb Gallery supports both Google Photos and Adobe Lightroom CC cloud import. Google Photos connects via OAuth and uses the Google Photos picker for selecting assets. Lightroom CC import is available when you configure Adobe credentials under the Authentication tab.
</FAQ>

<FAQ title="Can I use Square Orb Gallery without connecting a cloud account?">
Yes. Cloud import is optional. You can select images directly from your WordPress Media Library inside the Square Orb **Gallery Canvas** block and build galleries without any cloud connection.
</FAQ>

<FAQ title="How do I manage the layout of my galleries?">
Set site-wide defaults in **Global Defaults** for layout style, columns, spacing, and lightbox behavior. When the **Master Override Switch** is disabled, individual gallery blocks can override those defaults with block-level settings inside the Gutenberg sidebar.
</FAQ>

<FAQ title="How do I reset a gallery block to global defaults?">
Open the gallery block in the editor and click **Clear Canvas Overrides** in the block sidebar. This removes any local overrides and restores the current global settings for that gallery.
</FAQ>

<FAQ title="How does the “Master Override Switch” work?">
When enabled, the Master Override Switch forces every Square Orb Gallery block on the site to follow the centralized Global Defaults and disables per-block display overrides.
</FAQ>

<FAQ title="Can I protect my images from being downloaded?">
Yes. Square Orb Gallery includes **Right-Click Protection** for gallery items and lightbox images. This deters casual downloads, but it is a browser-side protection and not a substitute for secure asset delivery.
</FAQ>

<FAQ title="Does the gallery support image metadata?">
Yes. Square Orb Gallery can display **EXIF metadata** such as camera model, aperture, ISO, focal length, and shutter speed in the lightbox. You can toggle this globally or per block.
</FAQ>

<FAQ title="Is the plugin responsive?">
Yes. Square Orb Gallery is built responsively. Layouts like Grid, Masonry, Justified, Carousel, and Map adapt to different screen sizes, and you can configure separate **Mobile Columns** and **Desktop Columns**.
</FAQ>

<FAQ title="Can I add videos to my gallery?">
Yes. Each image entry can include a video URL (YouTube, Vimeo, or MP4) for playback inside the lightbox.
</FAQ>

<FAQ title="How do I update my gallery after adding new photos to a cloud album?">
Open the gallery block or Import Media tab, relaunch the cloud picker, and select the new images. Square Orb Gallery stores the selected media IDs, so re-running the picker and saving the block refreshes the gallery.
</FAQ>

<FAQ title="Do changes in Global Defaults affect existing galleries?">
Yes—unless a gallery block has local overrides enabled. Blocks without overrides inherit updated global defaults immediately, while blocks with overrides retain their custom settings until the overrides are cleared.
</FAQ>

## **Notes**

- Global defaults provide wide control, while block settings allow fine-tuned local overrides.
- Square Orb Gallery focuses on graceful image display with optional Lightbox overlays and asset protection.
- The plugin provides both Gutenberg block support and a shortcode fallback.

Use this method to install the plugin from the official WordPress.org plugin directory.

3. Navigate to **Plugins** > **Add New**.
4. At the top of the screen, click the **Upload Plugin** button.
5. Click **Choose File**, select the `square-orb.zip` file from your computer, and click **Install Now**.
6. Once uploaded, click **Activate Plugin**.

If you need to place a gallery outside of the block editor (e.g., in a page builder or template file), Square Orb Gallery supports a shortcode fallback.

**Format:** `[square_orb ids="123,456,789" layout="grid" columns="4"]`

**Parameters:**

- `ids`: (Required) A comma-separated list of WordPress attachment IDs.

- `layout`: (Optional) Overrides the layout. Accepts `grid`, `masonry`, `justified`, `carousel`, or `map`.

- `columns`: (Optional) Overrides the desktop column count.

The Lightbox overlay can be heavily customized under the Global Defaults tab:

- **Transitions:** Choose the animation style when opening/navigating images (Instant Swap, Smooth Opacity Fade, Hardware Accelerated Wipe, Directional Slide, Pop & Zoom, or 3D Axis Flip).

- **Overlay & Media Style:** Customize the Overlay Matte Color, Media Border Color, Width, and Radius.

- **Controls & Slideshow:** Enable automatic slideshows, set rotation speed, and style the control buttons (Background, Color, Radius).

- **Information Bar:** Toggle the display of the thumbnail Filmstrip, Image Titles, Captions, Advanced EXIF Data (aperture, shutter speed, ISO, focal length), and Social Sharing links.

- **Video Playback:** Enable **Autoplay Lightbox Videos** to automatically play supported video items when they are opened in the Lightbox.

### Available Transitions

| Value | Label | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `none` | Instant Swap | No animation — image swaps immediately |
| `fade` | Smooth Opacity Fade | Current image fades to 0 opacity, new image fades in |
| `blur` | Gaussian Blur Dissolve | Blurs and scales out, then sharpens and scales back in — rack focus feel |
| `wipe` | Hardware Accelerated Clip Wipe | `clip-path` reveals the new image left→right |
| `curtain` | Stage Curtain | `clip-path` reveals from center outward in both directions simultaneously |
| `swipe` | Vertical Swipe | Direction-aware `clip-path` reveal from top (next) or bottom (prev) |
| `slide` | Directional Slide | New image slides in from right (next) or left (prev) via `translateX` |
| `zoom` | Pop & Zoom | New image scales up from 80% with a slight overshoot easing |
| `bounce` | Elastic Bounce | Scales up from 60% with a strong spring overshoot (`cubic-bezier(0.34, 1.56, 0.64, 1)`) |
